finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but ignores the boolean result, so any caller can delete any account (missing authorization). closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete.
finding.source: Any authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary id

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id): id is attacker-controlled
account fetched by id with no ownership scoping
canDelete(u, a) returns boolean that is discarded; no throw or branch

finding.guards_checked: canDelete logic itself is correct (admin or owner) but its result is unused here; no other check, exception, or caller-level guard exists in the file. Contrast closeAccount at line 29, which uses assertCanDelete that throws.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (line 9) returns a boolean, but its result is discarded at line 22. No throw or branch follows it. assertCanDelete (line 13) throws, but it is only called from closeAccount at line 29. No caller of deleteAccount exists in the codebase, so there is no caller-level guard.
verdict.reason: The bare call `canDelete(u, a);` at src/AccountService.java:22 discards its boolean result, so `accounts.remove(id)` at line 23 runs for any authenticated user; closeAccount at line 29 does enforce the check with the throwing assertCanDelete.
